Feature request: Display cache write price in the Cost column of the Models management UI. The Cost (Credits per 1M Tokens) column in the Models management UI currently displays Input , Cache (read), and Output costs. However, the CAPI response also includes a field that is not surfaced anywhere in the UI. Example CAPI response fragment: Requested feature: Add a "Cache write" entry alongside the existing cost items (In, Cache, Out) in the Cost column so that users can see the full per-model pricing breakdown directly in the UI. - Show (and its long-context variant) from the CAPI response in the same format as the other cost fields (e.g. "Cache write: 625"). - Include it in hover tooltips (e.g. "Cache write: 625 credits per 1M tokens"). - When the value is missing or null, display a consistent fallback matching the behavior for other absent costs. - Support both default and long-context pricing rows in the model picker hover table. Why this matters: Cache write cost can be significantly higher than cache read cost (e.g. 625 vs 50 credits). Without this information in the UI, users cannot fully evaluate model pricing and may underestimate actual usage costs. The data is already returned by the API — it just needs to be displayed. Run in terminal tool returns 'Failed to retrieve command output' when output exceeds scrollback. Problem When a command's output exceeds the terminal's scrollback buffer ( , default 1000 lines), the tool returns "Failed to retrieve command output" instead of returning whatever is available in the buffer. Expected behavior The tool should return the full scrollback buffer contents (i.e. the last N lines that fit in scrollback) rather than failing entirely. Even partial output is more useful than an error message. Repro 1. Set to a low value (e.g. 100) 2. Have the agent run a command that produces more lines than the scrollback (e.g. ) 3. Tool result says "Failed to retrieve command output" Notes This is separate from the large output truncation/file-write handling in 321640 — that PR handles the case where output is successfully retrieved but exceeds the inline size limit. This issue is about output never being retrieved at all.

Agent terminal gets stuck on interactive package manager prompts (needrestart, debconf, pipe buffering). Summary The agent terminal tool fails to handle two classes of interactive prompts, causing consistent eval failures on terminalbench2 tasks that copilot-cli passes. Problem 1: needrestart/debconf TUI prompts When triggers needrestart, a "Which services should be restarted?" TUI prompt appears. None of the or patterns in match this format. The timer fires after 60s, the tool returns "moved to background", and the agent gives up. Example : — agent ran , needrestart prompted, agent waited 5 minutes then sent an empty and stopped. copilot-cli finished the same task in 33 seconds. Problem 2: Pipe buffering hides prompts When the model pipes an interactive command through / / , the pipe buffers all output until the upstream closes. Interactive prompts (like opam ) never reach the terminal buffer, so the cannot detect them. Example : — agent ran . The opam depext prompt was buffered by and never visible to the output monitor. The pattern would match if it reached the terminal — the bug is the pipe hiding it. Fix 1. Set in the copilot agent terminal env vars (in ), alongside existing , , etc. This prevents apt/dpkg from ever opening interactive prompts. 2. Add system prompt guidance telling the model to never pipe interactive commands through filters. Impact Found via terminalbench2 eval analysis comparing vscode-copilot-cli vs copilot-cli. These two issues account for 2 of 12 consistent regressions ( 13% score gap).

Repro (via smoke tests) 1. Open the Agents Window 2. Start a Claude session (warmup) — the session's workspace resolves to 3. After the warmup response, run 4. Expected : new-session homepage ( ) appears 5. Actual : error dialog, session stays active, homepage never appears This causes flaky failures in the and smoke tests in the Agents Window suite. The "Chat Sessions" suite (normal workbench) is unaffected. Root Cause passes to . When that URI uses a scheme no provider supports, throws, and the error propagates unhandled. Fix should catch the error from and fall through to the folder-less composer view (the new-session placeholder), rather than propagating the error. Repro Steps Turn on NVDA Open VS Code Azure left navigation "AML Infra – Engineering System” Machine learning tree grid item Observe the issue: Toolbar actions inside tree grid item are not discoverable and not programmatically associated for screen reader users Actual Result When focus is on the tree item (e.g., “AML Infra – Engineering System”), the screen reader announces the item’s name, state, and position but does not indicate that additional actions are available within the item. Users become aware of the toolbar only after pressing Tab, at which point it announces “tool bar” and the first button (e.g., “Filter button”). However, there is no programmatic relationship exposed between the tree item and its associated toolbar actions, causing a loss of context and making the actions non-discoverable. Expected Result When focus is on a tree item that contains inline actions, the screen reader should: - Indicate the presence of actions (e.g., “has actions” or “toolbar available”). - Clearly associate the toolbar with the parent tree item when focus moves to it (e.g., “Toolbar for AML Infra – Engineering System”). - Allow users to understand that the actions belong to the currently focused tree item without requiring trial-and-error navigation. Hidden secondary side bar should stay hidden when switching back to a session. Fixed via 320075. Bug In the Agents window, when a user hides the secondary side bar (auxiliary bar) for a session, switching away and back to that session would re-reveal the side bar, overriding the session's saved "hidden" state. This happened because restoring the session's editor working set reveals the editor part programmatically, which re-triggered the "editor implies auxiliary bar" invariant. Verification steps 1. Open the Agents window with at least two sessions, each having a file/editor open (e.g. open a file from files view so the editor + secondary side bar both show). 2. In session A, hide the secondary side bar (auxiliary bar). 3. Switch to session B, then switch back to session A. - ✅ The secondary side bar should remain hidden in session A. 4. In session B, keep the secondary side bar visible , switch to A and back to B. - ✅ The secondary side bar should remain visible in session B. 5. Open a file from files view in any session. - ✅ The editor and the secondary side bar should both be shown (invariant preserved for genuine editor reveals).

Agent host: "Trying to add a disposable to a DisposableStore that has already been disposed of" from in-process node.js file watcher. Seeing this error in the Main process output today, I think it shows when the window starts. Copilot flagged as related cc @DonJayamanne. I think it's harmless but just cleaning it up by fixing the disposable tracking. I'm just wondering whether the watcher churn can be reduced, I don't know anything about the area though. Copilot text below: Problem The agent host logs the following warning repeatedly: Root cause In ( ): is async. If the watcher instance is disposed while that promise is in flight, is already disposed by the time producing the warning and leaking the underlying handle.runs Why it shows up "a lot" in the agent host - The agent host runs the non-recursive node.js watcher in-process ( instantiates directly inside ), so the warning surfaces directly in agent host logs instead of a separate watcher process. - watches well-known customization roots (workspace root, , , , user home, agents/skills dirs) non-recursively and, on any relevant file change, tears down all those watchers and recreates them on the same paths (debounced). During an active session, files in the workspace root change frequently, so watchers are disposed and recreated exposing the race above.rapidly The watcher churn itself is by design (rescans pick up directories that appear later). The warning + leaked handle is the actual bug. Fix Use the existing helper so the resolved watch handle is disposed (instead of registered and leaked) when the watcher was disposed during the async . Possible follow-up (optional) disposes all watchers on every relevant change and rebuilds them, even for roots that didn't change. Diffing the root set would reduce the churn.

Performance: Cache getComputedStyle result in shadowCaretRangeFromPoint (mouse hot path). Problem In , the function calls six separate times to retrieve individual CSS font properties ( , , , , , ) and then concatenates them into a font shorthand string. Each call forces a synchronous style recalculation , which is expensive. Since this function runs on every mouse move over the editor viewport's shadow DOM content, the overhead is multiplied across every mousemove event in the editor. Fix Cache the result once in a local variable, then call on the cached result: Impact - 6x reduction in forced style recalculations on every mouse move over editor content - No functional change — identical output, same behavior - Low-risk, one-line addition, single file change File — function Related This is a well-known browser performance best practice — MDN recommends caching results when reading multiple properties:

[major] v1.123 breaks model-selection ability when resubmitting prompt. Regression: v1.123 breaks the ability to change the selected model with resubmitting a prompt. In this version the model used when resubmitting a prompt is no longer the model selected in the active editing field for the resubmitted prompt, but apparently erroneously tied to the "new prompt" selected model. 1. Submit a prompt in chat with Claude Opus 4.8, such as "Sing me a song." Wait for the response to complete. - Note in the response summary that the model used was Claude Opus 4.8. - Note also that the field for a new prompt also indicates Claude Opus 4.8, the same model that was just used. 2. Click the submitted prompt to edit it. Do not change the text, but change the model to GPT-5.5 and resubmit the prompt. Wait for the response to complete. 3. Look at the model that was used for the resubmitted prompt. Expected: GPT-5.5 was used for the resubmitted prompt. Actual: Claude Opus 4.8 was used for the resubmitted prompt. Conclusion: Even though the model was was changed to GPT-5.5 when resubmitting the prompt, GitHub Copilot ignored the newly selected model and resubmitted the prompt with the originally selected model. Workaround: Apparently the resubmitted prompt is no longer tied to the originally selected model, but to the selected model of the field for the new prompt. So you must change the model in the "new prompt" field before attempting to edit a submitted prompt. Discussion: Obviously this interrupts the workflow if you want to resubmit a prompt with a different model. Remembering to update the new prompt field is counterintuitive. It adds extra steps, and when you forget it burns credits. In addition this is an obvious regression; it worked before, and with the current bug the model selection UI when resubmitting a prompt serves no purpose, as it is broken.

Agent host CLI: kill running server leaks server node child process after upgrade. Summary The CLI agent host supervisor's path leaks the underlying server node process when restarting after a RPC. The bash launcher script ( ) is terminated, but the child it 'd remains alive as an orphan. Repro Discovered while testing against a remote macOS host using a pinned-old-server CLI: 1. Bring up an agent host supervisor on commit A (e.g. , protocol 0.2.0). 2. Connect a desktop on commit B (newer protocol 0.3.0). Handshake fails with . 3. Click "Update Server". The supervisor receives the RPC, calls , then restarts on commit B. 4. Observe processes on the remote: the bash wrapper for commit A is gone, but its node child (e.g. ) is still alive with . In my test run the orphan was pid 230 and survived indefinitely; only the new commit-B server's child was tracked by the supervisor after the restart. Suspected cause (or the platform-specific kill helper it delegates to) appears to signal the immediate child only. The server launcher is: Bash does not forward to its children by default, and we don't wait on it before terminating the new generation, so the node child is reparented to PID 1 and continues running. It does eventually exit when its IPC pipe closes, but in our test it persisted for the duration of the run. Suggested fix A couple of options, in rough order of preference: 1. Signal the whole process group / job from the CLI side — i.e. set up the server child in its own process group at spawn time ( / ) and send to the negative pgid on shutdown. Robust regardless of what the launch script does. 2. Make the launcher forward signals , e.g. / in and re-signal before . Cheaper change but doesn't help non-shell launchers. 3. Replace the bash launcher with a direct exec so the CLI's child is the node server. Simplest of all if there's no other reason to keep the shell shim. Scope - CLI only ( and the server-bin shim at ). - Independent of that PR fixes the desktop-side reconnect after upgrade, and is unaffected by whether the old server's node child gets reaped cleanly. - Probably also fires on any non-upgrade shutdown path that goes through (e.g. supervisor exit / quality switch), so the fix is generally useful. (Written by Copilot)

Recently Opened: deleted remote (WSL/SSH) folders are never removed from the list. Summary Deleted remote folders (e.g. opened via Remote - WSL) are never removed from File → Open Recent , even after you attempt to open them and the open fails because the path no longer exists. They stay in the top "workspaces/folders" section indefinitely. This is distinct from 74465 (closed by-design in 2019). There, the resolution was: "You can have many folders in your recents and we shouldn't hit the disk many times for each one when you open a vscode window. So instead if you try to open it and we find that it doesn't exist anymore, then we remove it from the list." That remove-on-open cleanup works for local folders, but it does not happen for remote ( ) folders - so a deleted WSL workspace lingers forever. I am not asking for a disk scan of every recent entry on startup (that's the perf concern from 74465); I'm reporting that the existing "remove it when we find it doesn't exist on open" behavior is missing for the remote case. Steps to Reproduce 1. In WSL, create a folder: 2. Open it in VS Code via Remote - WSL ( from the WSL shell). 3. Close the window. 4. Delete the folder in WSL: 5. Open VS Code and check File → Open Recent . Expected After attempting to open the now-missing remote folder (and VS Code finding it doesn't exist), the entry is removed from Open Recent — the same behavior 74465 says already happens for local folders. Actual The entry remains in Open Recent (top section) permanently. Attempting to open it surfaces an error, but the stale entry is not removed, so it keeps polluting the recent list and the quick-pick autocomplete. Notes - The entry persists across restarts; the only way to remove it via "Open Recent More ..." and then clicking "X". - Same problem is likely to affect other remote authorities (Remote - SSH, Dev Containers, Tunnels), since they share the remove-on-open path. Cross-file inline edit list never disposed; handleListEndOfLifetime not fired. Summary When the user accepts an inline edit whose target is a different document, the producing is never disposed. As a consequence, the extension-host callback never fires for cross-file inline edits, and any end-of-life telemetry the extension sends from that callback is silently dropped. This was caught while investigating missing telemetry for cross-file NES in the Copilot Chat extension. Steps to reproduce 0. Edit such that it becomes a recently-edited file such that it's included in NES context 1. Go to and change a symbol imported in , eg change to 2. You should get a cross-file NES suggesting to rename usage to in 3. :bug: Observe you don't get telemetry sent for this opportunity Expected: the extension provider receives for the cross-file list. Actual: it never fires. Diagnosis calls with no matching : constructs a whose ctor already calls on every item it holds and pairs it with in its dispose. The explicit is therefore redundant and leaks one ref on every cross-file accept, pinning the at forever. only runs when refCount hits 0, so → → never runs. I confirmed by adding temporary instrumentation to (per-instance id, captured stacks, a hook, a leak watchdog). The dump showed one leaked list per cross-file accept with an unpaired stack pointing at . was introduced in 290036 (commit ); the unpaired addRef has been there since that commit. Fix Drop the redundant in and add a cheap always-on invariant ( if refCount goes negative) to catch the inverse mistake. Fix in PR 318340.

Bug Report: tool silently fails on files (returns "success" but applies no changes). Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -- - VS Code Version: 1.121.0 - OS Version: Linux 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86 64 (WSL2 on Windows) When the Copilot Chat agent calls the tool against a file, the tool returns in every case, but the requested change is not applied. This affects all operation types: , (with a ), and with / . The misleading success message causes the agent to believe edits succeeded when they did not, leading to significant wasted effort and confused conversation state. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a moderately complex file in VS Code (the affected notebook has 24 cells, including cells with and outputs from / matplotlib). 2. Start a Copilot Chat agent session and ask the agent to edit a cell. 3. Have the agent call with a valid (verified valid via immediately before). 4. Observe that the tool returns . 5. Immediately call again — the cell's line range, count, and content are unchanged . 6. Verify on disk via / — file mtime and hash are also unchanged . Expected behavior - Either the edit is actually applied to the in-memory notebook buffer (and reflected in the next call), or - The tool returns a clear error message describing why the edit could not be applied. Actual behavior - The tool returns . - Disk is unchanged (mtime/hash identical). - In-memory buffer is unchanged (verified via on the open ). - shows identical cell count, IDs, and line ranges before/after. Diagnosis already performed The following potential causes were ruled out by controlled testing: | Hypothesis | Test | Result | |---|---|---| | Stale cell IDs from a prior context | Re-queried and used a freshly-returned ID | Still failed silently | | File-conflict state (notebook modified externally while open) | Ran and retried | Still failed silently | | Stale Copilot extension host | Ran and retried | Still failed silently | | Notebook metadata read-only flag | Inspected field — no or similar | Normal metadata | | Workspace/user settings override | No exists in the user data folder | Not the cause | | Single operation type bug | Tried , at cellId, at , at | All four silently failed | Possible triggers (unconfirmed) The notebook in question has features that may be related: - 24 cells, several with outputs (ipympl widgets) - Several cells with large embedded outputs - Had recently been modified externally (by a Python script that rewrote the JSON) while open in VS Code It is possible the silent failure is triggered by an unhandled exception inside the tool's edit application path that is being caught and converted to a success response. Suggested fix At minimum, the tool should return an actionable error when the edit cannot be applied — never a success message for a no-op. Ideally, the underlying cause (likely a model-buffer desync or an internal exception during the cell-replacement operation) should also be fixed. Workaround currently in use Closing the notebook in VS Code, editing the JSON directly via an external Python script, then reopening the notebook. This works reliably but defeats the purpose of having an agent-driven notebook editing tool.

Copilot Chat: Duplicate skills shown when using in input box due to symlinked skill directories. Summary When using in the Copilot Chat input box to reference skills, the same skills appear twice in the suggestions list. Steps to Reproduce 1. Install skills via — this installs skills to and also creates a symlink 2. Open VS Code with GitHub Copilot 3. In the Copilot Chat input box, type to trigger skill suggestions Result: Each skill appears twice in the dropdown. Expected Behavior Each skill should appear only once. Actual Behavior Skills are duplicated. VS Code scans both and as independent directories without realizing the latter is a symlink to the former. Root Cause (Hypothesis) VS Code scans multiple known skill directories independently without deduplication. When creates , both paths resolve to the same physical files, resulting in every skill being indexed and displayed twice. Suggested Fix When scanning skill directories, VS Code should: 1. Resolve symlinks before indexing, or 2. Deduplicate by resolved filesystem path ( / inode), or 3. Deduplicate by skill / identifier before rendering suggestions Additional Context intentionally creates as a symlink for Claude Code compatibility. Any user of on macOS/Linux will encounter this duplication in Copilot Chat.

Chronicle cloud sync: createCloudSession should gracefully handle policy-blocked users. Problem When enterprise policies block cloud session creation, the chronicle cloud sync repeatedly attempts to create sessions and fails. There is no caching of the policy-blocked state, so the same request is retried on every session start, generating unnecessary failures and eventually tripping the circuit breaker. Current behavior 1. User starts a chat session 2. Chronicle attempts createCloudSession 3. Server returns a policy-blocked error 4. Next session start: same thing repeats 5. After enough failures, circuit breaker trips (see 317330) 6. All cloud sync stops — including for users who might have mixed repos (some allowed, some not) Expected behavior 1. On first policy blocked response, cache the result with a TTL (e.g., 1 hour or until next window reload) 2. Skip createCloudSession attempts for that workspace/org during the TTL 3. Do not count policy blocked as a circuit breaker failure (it is an expected policy response, not a transient error) 4. Optionally surface a one-time notification: cloud sync is not available for this workspace due to organization policy Impact As chronicle rolls out more broadly, enterprise users with restrictive policies will see repeated silent failures. The current design conflates policy enforcement with infrastructure errors, causing the circuit breaker to trip unnecessarily. Suggested fix 1. Distinguish policy blocked from transient errors in the response handling 2. Cache the blocked state per-workspace with TTL 3. Exclude policy responses from the circuit breaker failure counter 4. Add a pre-flight check or early-exit before attempting createCloudSession when cached as blocked

Chronicle cloud sync: circuit breaker never recovers within a session. Problem The chronicle cloud sync circuit breaker transitions to an open (tripped) state after repeated failures, but never transitions back to a half-open or closed state within the same VS Code session. Once the breaker trips, cloud sync is effectively dead until the user restarts VS Code. There is no periodic retry or half-open probe to detect when the transient issue has resolved. Expected behavior The circuit breaker should implement a standard half-open state: - After a cooldown period (e.g., 5 minutes), attempt a single probe request - If the probe succeeds, transition back to closed and resume normal sync - If the probe fails, remain open and schedule the next probe with exponential backoff Current behavior - Circuit breaker opens after repeated failures (observed: 17 consecutive failures before trip) - Stays permanently open for the remainder of the session - User must restart VS Code to get cloud sync working again - No telemetry or notification informs the user that sync has stopped Impact Users in long-running sessions (common for remote/SSH developers) lose cloud sync for hours or days without realizing it. Their session history stops syncing silently. Suggested fix 1. Add a half-open state with periodic retry (e.g., exponential backoff starting at 5min, capped at 30min) 2. Emit telemetry when the breaker recovers (closed transition) to validate the fix 3. Consider a status bar indicator or notification when sync is degraded

Chronicle: SQLite store is unreliable on SSH-Remote workspaces. Problem The chronicle local store uses SQLite for persistence. On SSH-Remote workspaces (Linux), SQLite encounters cascading failures due to network filesystems not providing the POSIX locking guarantees that SQLite requires. The failure pattern is: 1. Initial locking protocol errors or disk I/O errors 2. Escalates to database disk image is malformed 3. Then file is not a database (corruption is now permanent) 4. All subsequent flush operations fail until the database file is deleted This disproportionately affects heavy users in remote development scenarios — exactly the cohort most reliant on session history. Observed error categories (flush operation) - database disk image is malformed — persistent corruption - file is not a database — corruption past recovery - locking protocol — concurrent access on non-POSIX FS - cannot rollback - no transaction is active — state desync - database is locked — contention Suggested mitigations 1. Detect remote filesystem and switch to WAL mode or a non-SQLite fallback (e.g., append-only JSON log) for workspaces where POSIX locking is not guaranteed 2. Auto-recover from corruption — detect malformed DB at init and recreate (with optional backup of raw data) 3. Add retry with backoff for transient locking errors before failing the flush Environment Primarily affects: Linux + SSH-Remote (vscode-server) Also observed in smaller numbers: Linux + tunnel connections

Webview extensions blank on Safari/WebKit (vscode.dev / code-server / code serve-web): VSBuffer.slice returns view that gets detached by extension-host postMessage transfer. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -- VS Code Version Reproduced against code-server (vendoring ). Bug exists in current per source inspection of and . Per the introducing commit (microsoft/vscode 76076) it has been present since 2019. OS Version - Server : Ubuntu 24.04, Node 20.x - Clients (reproduces) : Safari 18 on macOS 15, Safari 18 on iPadOS 18, Chrome / Brave / Firefox on iOS (all forced WebKit by App Store policy) - Clients (does not reproduce) : Chrome / Chromium / Brave / Edge on macOS / Linux / Windows (V8), Firefox desktop (SpiderMonkey) Does this reproduce in native VS Code desktop? No. Native VS Code (Electron) uses Electron's IPC layer between renderer and extension host — not browser with transfer lists for payloads. The underlying is never detached in that flow, so 's held subarray views stay valid and 's view-returning behavior is correct. The bug is specifically a browser-mode VS Code issue. Does this reproduce in ? Yes (architecturally identical, not directly stood up). ships the same code path and the same browser-based web-worker extension host. Any Safari / iOS client of should hit it identically. Reproduces deterministically in , which vendors the same upstream code verbatim. Does this reproduce in ? Likely yes. I have not directly tested in Safari since is harder to drive a webview-heavy extension on (the marketplace surface is narrower). Long-standing issue 213143 ("Safari 14 no longer able to load vscode.dev") and adjacent reports point in the same direction. Same upstream code path. Does this reproduce in GitHub Codespaces? Likely yes (Codespaces uses VS Code web). Not directly tested. Steps to Reproduce 1. Run any browser-mode VS Code (vscode.dev, , code-server, Codespaces) over HTTPS — service workers must register. 2. Activate any extension that delivers initial webview content as multi-chunk binary IPC frames. Reliable repro: Claude Code ( version specifically; newer versions hit an unrelated Anthropic-side regression that masks this bug). Alternative repros that hit the same code path: vscode-pdf (open a PDF), notebook renderers (open a notebook with rendered output), Live Preview. 3. Open in Safari (macOS or iPadOS) or any iOS browser. Open Web Inspector → Console. 4. Click the extension's activity-bar icon to open its webview panel. 5. Panel stays permanently blank. Console fires the cascade below. 6. Confirm it does NOT reproduce on V8: open the same URL in Chrome / Edge on macOS / Linux / Windows. Panel renders normally. Errors from the Dev Tools Console …fires once per IPC chunk on the management socket, then again on the extension-host socket. The cascade kills the channel; any subsequent IPC traffic for the extension is dead until reload. --- Root cause ( ) currently returns: This is a view into the parent , not a copy — a deliberate perf optimization from 76076. The new 's . In , queues incoming chunks and uses to extract messages: Both and the residual chunk are views over the same that arrived in the WebSocket binary frame. Downstream, the extracted message is delivered to the web-worker extension host iframe via . The list detaches the underlying in the originating window. still holds chunks whose is now a view into a detached . The next read calls on that view. - V8 (Chromium / Node / Electron) is permissive about this. Historically on a view of a detached buffer returned an empty buffer; modern V8 throws, but the timing of the detach vs. the read is loose enough that the bug rarely fires in practice. This is why the bug is essentially invisible on every desktop browser and on Electron. - JavaScriptCore (Safari, iOS browsers) throws synchronously and unconditionally per . The IPC reader unwinds, fires, the channel is dead. The detach-then-read race only fires for messages that need to be sliced (multi-chunk read) AND get transferred immediately downstream (webview content delivery). Routine editor traffic is single-chunk and short-lived, so it never hits the race. Webview-heavy extensions hit it on their very first frame. --- Candidate fixes (ranked by blast radius) A. Make copy unconditionally (simplest, broadest) - Pros : one-character source change; semantics-correct in all environments; fully reversible; restores the pre- 76076 contract. - Cons : walks back the perf optimization in all environments, including desktop Electron where the bug is invisible. Cost: one per call. Sub-kilobyte typical IPC message sizes; in benchmarks against a sustained extension-host workload (Claude Code session, multiple notebook renderers) I haven't been able to measure the regression above noise, but I'm flagging it. I'd open this as a Draft RFC PR alongside this issue. If maintainers prefer B or C below, easy to rewrite. B. Make copy only in web/browser bundles (perf-preserving) Use the existing / / source layout to split implementations: (Or via a build-target conditional that swaps the implementation file.) - Pros : zero perf impact on desktop Electron where the bug is invisible; only the affected platform pays the copy cost. - Cons : introduces platform-conditional semantics for a primitive that should arguably behave the same everywhere. Asymmetric semantics is a footgun for future contributors. C. Copy at the IPC reader, not in (most surgical) Have produce owned buffers regardless of semantics: - Pros : minimum semantic blast radius; the rest of the codebase keeps the view-returning for everywhere else. - Cons : more code; doesn't fix the same class of bug if it surfaces in any other code path that holds a view across a transferable boundary (and there are several such paths — anywhere a is held while another caller might post the original). I believe (C) is partial: it cures the symptom in the IPC reader specifically, but the underlying contract violation ( returns a view that can outlive its source's lifecycle) remains lurking elsewhere. Fine if maintainers want the minimum change; (A) is the more durable fix. --- Verifying the fix A regression test that fails before (A) and passes after, suitable for : is in V8 since Chrome 114 (May 2023) and Node 21.7. If the runtime VS Code targets for unit tests is older, the test can use or instead, with the same semantic effect. --- Production validation We've been running fix (A) — applied as a one-character to the bundled post-install — in production across three independent code-server deployments for 24h. Before the patch, every webview-heavy extension session on Safari/iPad fired the cascade and stayed blank. After the patch, all WebKit clients work normally with no observable side effects or perf regressions. The same patch on V8 clients is a no-op (Chromium was already working). Patch site in the minified bundle (offset confirmed at column 97282 of line 406 in for code-server's vendored 1.107.x build): If maintainers want a self-contained Docker Compose reproducer (code-server + minimal extension + the broken-on-WebKit state vs. the patched-and-working state, with HAR captures), I'm happy to set one up. --- Why this matters Every Safari and iOS user of browser-based VS Code is currently locked out of every webview-heavy extension. That includes: - users on Safari (long surface, hard to deterministically repro outside of a binary-protocol extension). - All deployments — disproportionately the population that hits this, because code-server is browser-only and the iPad/iOS audience is large among self-hosted dev environments. - and Codespaces users on Safari/iOS. Proposal Make all built-in tools always available in every request. - Built-in tools contributed by the Copilot Chat extension are stable per session and do not register/unregister at runtime. - Extension-contributed tools can remain deferred or be handled separately. Symptom Across two consecutive chat requests in the same session, the entire 9.7k-token system block is byte-identical except for a single 9-character substring inside the listing: The system-level prompt cache breakpoint sits at the end of the system block, so this single-line mutation invalidates the entire system prefix. Listener leak in Getting Started page: onDidChangeConfiguration registered inside onDidProgressStep callback. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.120.0 (main branch, commit 89fc6394f59) - OS Version: All platforms Bug In (the Welcome/Walkthrough editor), a listener for is registered inside the event callback using . Each time a walkthrough step is completed, a new permanent configuration listener accumulates in the disposable store and is never cleaned up. After completing N walkthrough steps across any walkthroughs, N identical listeners exist, each toggling the same CSS class on every config change. This grows without bound for the lifetime of the editor. This is the exact anti-pattern the project's own warn about: Do NOT register a disposable to the containing class if the object is created within a method that is called repeatedly to avoid leaks. Instead, return an IDisposable from such method and let the caller register it. Affected code File: Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the Welcome tab (Getting Started page) 2. Complete several walkthrough steps (e.g., toggle "Choose your Theme", "Rich Language Support", etc.) 3. Each step completion fires , which registers a new listener 4. After completing 10 steps, there are 10 identical config listeners in the disposable store 5. These listeners remain until the Getting Started editor is closed 6. Reopening the Getting Started editor and completing more steps adds more listeners Impact - Memory grows linearly with walkthrough step completions - Each redundant listener runs on every configuration change event, wasting CPU - Users who explore multiple walkthroughs accumulate dozens of dead listeners Fix A PR is available: 314636 The fix moves the subscription to the constructor, alongside the other config/event listeners, so it is registered exactly once.

(Codex) Problem The Copilot CLI chat-panel path preserves editor selection context when sending a request: it forwards the selected file, selected text, and selection range. The Agent Host path currently converts an implicit selection into a selection attachment, but only includes the file URI and display name. The selected text and range are dropped before the request reaches the Copilot SDK. Current Context There are incoming agent host protocol changes for richer attachments. This issue should track the VS Code-side implementation work after those changes land, rather than extending the current older / / attachment shape directly. Evidence - - handles implicit selections, but emits only today. - - already has optional and fields in the current VS Code-side interface. - - already forwards and to the public Copilot SDK if present. - - The existing chat-panel CLI path preserves richer selection context. Expected Behavior When a user sends a Copilot CLI request through Agent Host with editor selection context, the Agent Host path should preserve: - selected file URI/path - selected text - selection start/end line and character This should match the current Copilot CLI chat-panel behavior and avoid losing important context after moving CLI integration to Agent Host. Likely Fix After the richer attachment shape lands, wire editor selection attachments through the VS Code Agent Host path: - Convert implicit editor selection variables into the richer selection attachment shape. - Preserve selected text and selection range when converting chat variables in . - Preserve those fields through Agent Host side effects/state. - Map the richer Agent Host selection attachment into the Copilot SDK selection attachment shape in . Classification Agent Host implementation gap. The public Copilot SDK already accepts selection and fields; the remaining work is VS Code-side Agent Host wiring after the incoming agent host protocol changes land.

Menu Translation Missing in Custom Title Bar (Possible NLS Regression). Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -- - VS Code Version: 1.118.1 - OS Version: Windows 11 25H2 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Use a non-English language pack (e.g. Chinese). 2. Open VS Code with default settings (window.titleBarStyle = custom). 3. Observe the main menu items — some entries (e.g. "Selection", "Go") appear in English instead of translated. 4. Set "window.titleBarStyle": "native" and reload the window. 5. Observe that the same menu items are now correctly translated. Expected Behavior Menu items should be consistently localized regardless of window.titleBarStyle. Actual Behavior When using the custom title bar, some menu items fall back to English. Switching to native title bar restores correct translations. Additional Context This appears to be a regression potentially introduced by 311927. Based on investigation of the NLS pipeline: Relocating localize calls can change the generated NLS message indices Language packs depend on stable metadata/index mapping This may result in mismatched or missing translations at runtime The issue seems specific to the custom title bar implementation path, suggesting different menu rendering code paths may be using inconsistent NLS mappings.
